1.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines “Kekerasan Terhadap Perempuan” broadly as violence occurring in the private or public sphere (Pasal 1 angka 13: “baik yang terjadi di ranah privat atau publik”), and defines “Rumah Tangga” (Pasal 1 angka 19), but it does not explicitly name or regulate “kekerasan dalam rumah tangga”/domestic violence/intimate partner violence as a distinct category. The retrieved English passages likewise only list general forms of violence (fisik/psikis/seksual/ekonomi) and general prevention/services. The judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with what is actually written; therefore the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be an over-interpretation of ‘private sphere’ language rather than an explicit domestic-violence provision.

Prevention of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women shall be implemented in an integrated and coordinated manner coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal.
7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.
12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threat of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms.
13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances.
15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty.
22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims.
23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution.
24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life.
25. Integrated Service is the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination.
26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizer to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family.
31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection.
32. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life.
34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
35. Village/Sub-District Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women and children protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

1.10.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly includes technology-facilitated violence. Pasal 1 angka 17 defines “Kekerasan Seksual” to include “kekerasan seksual berbasis elektronik,” and Pasal 6 ayat (2) huruf g provides a right to “penghapusan konten bermuatan seksual untuk kasus kekerasan seksual dengan media elektronik.” These are direct references to electronic/online sexual violence and related remedies. The judge correctly cited these. Therefore the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.

4.3.rationale: The retrieved candidates contain explicit legal/policy awareness language tied to preventing violence/exploitation/discrimination. In the Indonesian source, Pasal 9 ayat (4) huruf b states: “melakukan sosialisasi mengenai peraturan perundang-undangan yang berkaitan dengan pelindungan hak perempuan,” within the section “Pencegahan Kekerasan, Eksploitasi dan Diskriminasi.” This is reasonably an awareness/education activity about relevant laws/regulations in the VAW prevention context. The judge was overly strict by requiring the text to say ‘VAW laws’ as a separate phrase, even though the prevention article is explicitly about violence/exploitation/discrimination against women.

5.3.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences mention community leaders and local cultural organizations, but they do not explicitly reference traditional/customary leaders, customary institutions, or customary dispute-resolution mechanisms as such.

Article 33
(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business entities and other related stakeholders.
(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;
b. taking preventive measures against violence against women; and
c. conducting skills training.

Article 21
What is meant by related agencies are agencies that have a role in the implementation of women's empowerment in the field of national unity and politics, as well as other agencies and institutions including the General Election Commission, the Election Supervisory Board, political organizations, and communities organized in political parties, non-governmental organizations, women's associations or organizations, universities or research institutions, as well as mass media.

Article 22
What is meant by related agencies are agencies that have a role in the implementation of women's empowerment in the social field, which may include women and child protection institutions, legal aid organizations and assistance for victims of violence, safe houses (shelters) that handle victims of gender-based violence, psychology practitioners and counselors, universities/educational institutions, community organizations, Family Welfare Empowerment, gender study centers at universities, family counseling consultation institutions, religious organizations that have women's empowerment programs, social rehabilitation centers.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by respect for human rights is respect, upholding the inherent human rights of citizens, as well as protecting dignity and worth as human beings.
Letter b What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing tribe, religion, belief, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or actions toward vulnerable women's groups with the aim that they obtain equal rights is not included as an act of discrimination.
Letter c What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to women as well as men.
What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that describes equal, harmonious and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.
Letter d What is meant by benefit is the implementation of women's protection that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

6.11.rationale: The Indonesian regulation explicitly includes “perempuan pekerja rumah tangga” (domestic workers) as a vulnerable group (Pasal 9 ayat (3) huruf g). As with other vulnerable groups, Pasal 9 ayat (2) and Pasal 9 ayat (4) (especially huruf n on special protection/support systems for vulnerable groups) indicate that prevention and special support are intended to cover these groups. The judge’s ‘No’ is driven by demanding domestic-worker-specific measures, but the indicator (domestic workers) is satisfied by explicit inclusion as a vulnerable group within the prevention/protection framework.
